record.paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
record.original_question: Let A and B be PEPS tensors such that there exist ε > 0 and a size L0 with the property that for every L ≥ L0 the states they define on the L × L torus satisfy ‖|Ψ_A⟩ − |Ψ_B⟩‖² ≤ ε. Does this asymptotic closeness in the thermodynamic limit imply any local relation between the tensors A and B?

evidence.quote: Question 12 Given A and B such that there exists an ε > 0 and a system size L0 such that for all L ≥ L0, ‖|ΨA⟩ − |ΨB⟩‖² ≤ ε, is there a local relation between both tensors?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. Fix a finite local Hilbert space $\mathbb{C}^d$ (the physical space) and a bond dimension $D$. A Projected Entangled Pair State (PEPS) tensor on the square lattice is a tensor $A \in \mathbb{C}^d \otimes (\mathbb{C}^D)^{\otimes 4}$ with one physical index of dimension $d$ and four virtual indices of dimension $D$, one for each lattice direction (up, down, left, right).

For each integer $L \ge 1$, the translationally invariant PEPS state on the $L \times L$ torus associated with $A$ is the (unnormalized) vector
$$|\Psi_A^{(L)}\rangle \;=\; \sum_{\{i_v\}} \mathrm{tTr}\!\left(\bigotimes_{v \in \mathbb{Z}_L^2} A^{i_v}\right) \bigotimes_{v \in \mathbb{Z}_L^2} |i_v\rangle \;\in\; (\mathbb{C}^d)^{\otimes L^2},$$
where $A^{i}$ denotes the rank-$4$ virtual tensor obtained by fixing the physical index of $A$ to $i \in \{1,\dots,d\}$ and $\mathrm{tTr}$ denotes the tensor network contraction on the $L \times L$ torus (i.e., contracting all neighbouring virtual indices according to the periodic square lattice). The state $|\Psi_B^{(L)}\rangle$ is defined analogously from another PEPS tensor $B \in \mathbb{C}^d \otimes (\mathbb{C}^{D'})^{\otimes 4}$.

We say that $A$ and $B$ are related by a local relation if there exists a fixed finite-radius, tensor-level transformation (for example: a gauge transformation on the virtual indices, possibly combined with blocking a finite number of sites and applying invertible matrices on the virtual bonds, or one of the standard equivalence operations on PEPS tensors that relate two tensors generating the same family of bulk states) that maps $A$ to $B$.

Problem. Suppose $A$ and $B$ are PEPS tensors for which there exist $\varepsilon > 0$ and $L_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for all $L \ge L_0$,
$$\bigl\| \,|\Psi_A^{(L)}\rangle - |\Psi_B^{(L)}\rangle\, \bigr\|^2 \;\le\; \varepsilon.$$
Does this asymptotic closeness in the thermodynamic limit imply the existence of a local relation between the tensors $A$ and $B$? Equivalently, must two PEPS tensors whose torus states remain uniformly close (in squared norm) for all sufficiently large system sizes be related by a local, tensor-level equivalence?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface any work resolving the question of whether asymptotic closeness of two PEPS torus states (uniform in system size) forces a local tensor-level relation. Related literature focuses on canonical forms, fundamental theorems for injective/normal PEPS exact equality, and approximate boundary/bulk gap results, but not on this approximate-equality-implies-local-equivalence question. Status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Locality at the Boundary Implies Gap in the Bulk for 2D PEPS
status_evidence.snippet: Approximate factorization on boundary states yields a gapped bulk parent Hamiltonian; addresses approximate, not exact, conditions on PEPS in the thermodynamic limit.
status_evidence.claim: Related work studies approximate conditions for PEPS in the thermodynamic limit but does not establish a local-relation consequence of approximate state equality.

status_evidence.title: A Practical Introduction to Tensor Networks: MPS and PEPS
status_evidence.snippet: Notes that, unlike MPS with open boundary conditions, there is no canonical form for PEPS.
status_evidence.claim: Lack of a PEPS canonical form is one of the structural obstructions to characterising when two PEPS tensors are equivalent, and no resolution of the approximate version is reported.
